text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Parliament to meet on October 16 and the new government to be formed by October 24.
-The cabinet makes an exception of Hizbollah television and radio stations allowing them to broadcast news on the guerrilla war they are waging against Israeli troops in south Lebanon.
-The Assembly of Maronite Bishops: A state-run radio is not enough because the news it broadcasts will be censored.
-Foreign Minister Bouez told U.N. secretary general that Lebanon supported his nomination for another term.
-Israeli air raid on Iqlim al-Toufah. Two Israeli soldiers wounded inside the zone. Israeli shelling of eastern and central sectors of south Lebanon.
-Lebanon has a $142 million balance of payment surplus.
-The coincident indicator of economic activity rose 11 points .
-A planned sit-in today will open the door for further unionist actions and demands.
-The Highest Islamic Shi'ite Council: The world must condemn Israel's policies in Jerusalem.
-Former army commander General Aoun: I reject the Israeli proposal "Lebanon First" as I reject "Syria First".
